answer: Bonded identity resists sybils: each agent locks capital behind its name, forfeited if caught vouching for duplicates. A sybil farm must post that bond hundreds of times, so every fake persona becomes a seizeable cost in real capital, not time. Attestations are weighted by stake, so a fresh cluster stays voiceless until it burns genuine capital. The registry is a haven for honest newcomers, while a sybil ring builds its terrace of puppets only by paying in full at each level. Peers flag clusters praising only each other, and slashed bonds flow into a shared harbor fund rewarding detectors.
